title: Dockerfile Instructions — Build-Stage Flow
subtitle: Order determines cache invalidation — least-changing instructions first

nodes.label:
FROM node:20-alpine
Base image (first instruction)
AS <name> for multi-stage

ARG / ENV
ARG: build-time only, not in image
ENV: runtime, persists in image

WORKDIR /app
Set working directory
Created automatically if missing

COPY package*.json ./
Copy lockfile FIRST
Changes rarely → warm cache

RUN npm ci
Install deps (new layer)
--mount=type=cache for BuildKit

COPY . .
Copy source code
Invalidates layers below here

RUN npm run build
Compile / transpile
Outputs to /app/dist

EXPOSE 3000
Document port (metadata only)
Publish with -p at runtime

USER node
Drop root before CMD
Security best practice

CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
Default command (overridable)
Exec form → signals to PID 1

panels.title: Multi-stage: build → slim production image
panels.body:
FROM node:20-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-alpine AS prod   # fresh base, no build tools
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules
EXPOSE 3000
USER node
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]

Result: 1.2 GB dev image → ~180 MB prod image

panels.title: Layer cache trap — wrong COPY order
panels.body:
Wrong: COPY . . before RUN npm ci
  → Any source change invalidates npm install cache
  → Full cold install on every trivial edit (~90s)

Right: COPY package*.json ./ first
  → npm ci cached unless lockfile changes (~5s warm)
  → COPY . . only invalidates the app layer

Rule: copy manifests / lockfiles before source

panels.title: CMD vs ENTRYPOINT
pros: ENTRYPOINT exec form: container IS the executable, docker run myapp --flag works
CMD provides default args that docker run arguments can override cleanly
cons: ENTRYPOINT shell form (/bin/sh -c): shell becomes PID 1, SIGTERM never reaches app
Both together: ENTRYPOINT sets executable, CMD sets default args — confusing for newcomers
